title: Stuffed peppers
subtitle: Peppers filled with seasoned beef mince, rice, and tomato sauce
excerpt: Stuffed peppers are hollowed-out red or green peppers packed with a filling of beef mince, rice, onion, and tomato, then baked in the oven until the peppers are tender and the filling is cooked through. Each pepper is a self-contained portion. A simple, crowd-pleasing weeknight dinner.
sourceNotes: American home-cooking tradition. Stuffed peppers appear in Fannie Farmer, The Boston Cooking-School Cook Book (1896), Project Gutenberg, and became a staple of mid-century American cookbooks including Joy of Cooking.

recipe.freezeNotes: Bake from frozen at 180°C for 45 minutes covered with foil, then uncovered for 10 minutes.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Assemble up to a day ahead and refrigerate unbaked. Add 10 minutes to the baking time.

content.text: Stuffed peppers are whole peppers, tops removed and seeds cleared, filled with seasoned beef mince, par-cooked rice, and a tomato sauce, then baked until the pepper walls are soft and the filling is cooked through. Each pepper makes one portion. The meat and rice filling can be assembled while the oven heats.

items.prepNote: tops sliced off and seeds removed

content.text: Heat the oven to 190°C. Heat {{vegetable-oil}} of oil in the frying pan over medium-high heat. Brown {{beef-mince}} of beef mince, breaking it up, for 5 minutes. Add {{onion}} onion and cook for 3 minutes. Add {{garlic}} of garlic, {{tomato-puree}} of tomato purée, and {{italian-seasoning}} of Italian seasoning. Cook for 1 minute.

Add half the {{tinned-tomatoes}} of chopped tomatoes and {{worcestershire-sauce}} of Worcestershire sauce. Simmer for 5 minutes. Stir in the par-cooked {{long-grain-rice}} of rice. Season well. The filling should be moist but not watery.

Stand the {{pepper-red}} peppers upright in a deep roasting tin. Spoon the remaining chopped tomatoes into the base of the tin with 100 ml of water. Pack the filling firmly into each pepper. Scatter {{cheddar}} of grated cheddar on top if using.

Cover the tin tightly with foil. Bake for 35 minutes. Remove the foil and bake for a further 15 minutes until the peppers are tender and the top is golden. Rest for 5 minutes before serving, spoon the tomato pan sauce around.

items.symptom: Peppers collapsing and not standing upright
items.cause: Unstable base or peppers too soft before baking.
items.fix: Choose peppers with flat bases and similar size. Trim a tiny slice off the base if needed to level them.
Par-cook the rice for at least 7 minutes so it is almost done before going into the pepper.

content.text: A vegetarian version replaces the beef with cooked lentils or a mix of black beans and sweetcorn. Turkey or chicken mince both work. Green peppers give a more bitter, less sweet result. Adding a handful of chopped olives or feta to the filling changes the register entirely.

Stuffed peppers are a mid-twentieth-century American family dinner staple. They appear in Joy of Cooking and nearly every American general cookbook from the postwar period. Each pepper is its own meal, which is useful when people want different amounts.
